summary: Located in a popular upper Eden Valley village, 20 minutes from the centre of Penrith, a well presented, Grade II listed, sympathetically extended, former coaching inn, with flexible and spacious living accommodation, 3 bedrooms, generous mature gardens and private cobbled courtyard with barn.
description:
Occupying a prominent central position within this charming Upper Eden Valley village, as its name suggests, The Old Sun Inn is a detached Grade II listed former Coaching Inn dating back to the early 1800s.

Rich in character and history, the property has been extended to the rear and sympathetically refurbished in recent years to provide spacious and versatile three-bedroom accommodation, whilst retaining a wealth of original features.

Following a traditional Georgian "four square" layout, the property is entered via a recessed porch leading into a central entrance hall with part-panelled walls, a coved ceiling and an understairs cloakroom.

There are three generous reception rooms, including a charming living room with a log-burning stove, tiled hearth, original pitch pine floorboards and a sash window. A separate study/sitting room offers a cosy retreat, complete with window seat, shutters and access to the cellar, while a third reception room provides flexible living space with an open fire, fitted cupboards and shelving, sash window with shutters and a cast iron radiator.

The kitchen has been thoughtfully redesigned by Atlantis Kitchens of Kendal and fitted with a range of contemporary wall and base units, an inset sink, central island and integrated appliances, including a dishwasher and fridge/freezer. A feature fireplace recess houses the hob with a pop-up extractor, complemented by Karndean flooring, recessed lighting and useful understairs storage.

To the rear, the property has been extended into the former coach house creating a striking dining hall/garden room provides a bright and sociable space, featuring pine floorboards, halogen lighting, a half-pitched glazed roof and French doors opening to both sides. Beyond this is a highly useful boot/utility room, formerly a stable and still retaining its original stall divisions, which adds practicality and provides access to the courtyard. Stairs rise from here to a mezzanine room above, ideal for use as an office or studio, with a vaulted ceiling and exposed timbers.

Upstairs, the main house offers three well-proportioned bedrooms. The principal bedroom benefits from fitted wardrobes and a pleasant dual aspect. A beautifully appointed bathroom completes the accommodation, featuring a cast iron roll-top bath, separate shower, heritage-style fittings and dual-aspect windows.

Externally, the property enjoys a generous and well-stocked mature garden, along with an enclosed cobbled courtyard. There are three useful store rooms and a substantial lofted barn offering excellent storage or workshop potential, with scope for conversion subject to the necessary consents.

Skirwith is a picturesque and unspoilt village surrounded by the beautiful countryside of the Pennine Area Of Outstanding Natural Beauty, approximately two miles from the foot of Cross Fell and around eight miles north-east of Penrith. The Lake District National Park is also within easy reach, just a 20-minute drive away. The nearby village of Langwathby provides a selection of amenities and village store and a well-regarded primary school. Further schooling is available in Culgaith and Penrith, both of which are served by a school bus network.

This is a rare opportunity to acquire a truly distinctive village home, combining generous accommodation, period charm and attractive outdoor space in one of Cumbria’s most desirable rural locations.

Directions From Penrith follow the A686 through Langwathby taking the next right hand turn signposted for Skirwith.

In the village the property is facing the T-junction.
